stem.text: Let f be a continuous function with \( f(1) = -2 \), \( f(2) = 5 \). Let \( g(x) = \int_{x^{2} - 3}^{4} f(t) \, dt \). Find the value of \( g'\left(2\right) \).

worked_solution.text: Reversing the limits, \( g(x) = -\int_{4}^{x^{2} - 3} f(t) \, dt \), so by the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus its derivative is minus the integrand evaluated at \( x^{2} - 3 \).
The chain rule multiplies by the derivative of \( x^{2} - 3 \), which is \( 2 x \).
At \( x = 2 \) the limit is \( 1 \) and its derivative is \( 4 \).
